transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Zhao (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions), Sarah Lim (Horizon Head of ML), Carlos Mendes (Platform), Priya Rao (Security), Tom Brenner (SRE)

Summary:
Horizon DataWorks runs a customer-facing embeddings/search product and wants token-level tracing of LLM inference to attribute latency/cost to customer queries, plus integration into their OpenTelemetry pipeline. Main asks: token path visibility (per-request per-token spans), sampling strategy, how KV cache and batching appear in traces, and constraints around VPC/private deployment and KMS/HSM. They want a pilot with staging trace capture and benchmarking dashboards.

Topics Covered:
- Token-level spans and span structure for Redwood runtime
- OpenTelemetry/OTLP ingestion patterns and collector configuration
- Span sampling vs. tail-sampling for long-running generations
- KV cache hits/misses instrumentation and heatmap metrics
- Batching visibility and batch-id propagation in traces
- Quantized model performance signals and per-kernel timing
- VPC/private agent connectivity & KMS/HSM considerations
- Dashboarding: per-route latency, token-cost, heatmaps, and SLO alerts

Action Items (captured): see metadata action_items field above

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: morning everybody thanks for making time, um we're going to jump into token level instrumentation and how that ties into your OTEL pipeline, Ethan will drive the runtime bits, I'll cover rollout/contract, and Lena will touch on dashboards.
[00:22] Sarah Lim: thanks Maya, quick context: we have a search product serving retail recommendations, average generation lengths around 120 tokens but some long-form completions hit 1.5k tokens. Cost attribution is messy today.
[00:35] Ethan Zhao: right, and the key here is we instrument at two layers: per-request orchestration spans, and an inner per-token or per-chunk span emitted by the runtime. We avoid emitting a span per token by default, that's noisy; instead we emit token-path spans at configurable granularity, e.g., every 8 tokens or at model-phase boundaries.
[01:08] Carlos Mendes: when you say "model-phase boundaries" can you clarify? is that attention/kvs or is that like forward/backward?
[01:14] Ethan Zhao: good question — by phase I mean logical steps inside the step: kv-cache lookup, attention kernel, sampling/logits, plus prefix cache prefetch. Those are tagged in spans as kind: "kv-lookup", "attn-kernel", "sampling".
[01:39] Tom Brenner: how do we see batching? our platform uses both micro-batching and dynamic batching on the GPU. We need to attribute latency to customer requests within a batch.
[01:48] Ethan Zhao: we propagate a batch_id in trace baggage and create child spans for batch assembly and dispatch. Each request gets a short 'enqueue' span and then a 'batch-dispatch' span with tags for batch_size and wait_time_ms. Inside the runtime we annotate per-request token spans with the batch index. That allows us to break down latency per-request even though they hit the same kernel call.
[02:20] Sarah Lim: any concerns about trace volume? emitting per-token spans will explode our storage.
[02:28] Lena Ortiz: yes that's why we recommend a sampling policy: low-rate full-token sampling for long contexts, head-only sampling for short requests, plus adaptive tail-sampling to catch long tails and regressions. Also prefix/KV cache metrics are aggregated counters to avoid per-token duplication.
[03:01] Priya Rao: from security side we need to know what leaves our VPC. Are you sending raw tokens to Redwood-hosted collectors? our policy prohibits any PII egress.
[03:11] Maya Patel: good call — for Private/VPC deployments the OTLP exporter can be inside your VPC and talk to your collector. Redwood can run an agent inside the private network that only emits metadata and hashed token ids if needed. Plain text tokens do not leave unless you opt-in for content-level tracing. We also support KMS integrations and HSM for key wrapping.
[03:47] Priya Rao: ok, and audit logs? we need deterministic retention, SOC2 controls.
[03:52] Maya Patel: we provide audit logs and can configure retention to match your policy; SOC2 is available for Redwood Dedicated and Private tiers, and we can include the compliance package in the pilot proposal.
[04:18] Carlos Mendes: can you show an example OTLP pipeline? collector config we run is a fluent-collector -> otel-collector -> splunk/elastic.
[04:25] Ethan Zhao: sure, high-level: runtime -> local sidecar exporter -> otel collector (batch_transform) -> tail-sampler -> processor for attribute enrichment -> backend. We'll share an example config that plugs into your pipeline. Note: pay attention to batch/queue sizes on the collector to avoid backpressure.
[05:05] Sarah Lim: about KV cache hit/miss — we want a heatmap per model + route to spot cold prefixes. How do you recommend instrumenting that?
[05:14] Ethan Zhao: runtime emits histogram of prefix-latency and a KV-cache metric with labels: model, shard, prefix_hash(mod 100), hit=true/false. The heatmap is computed in the metrics backend by bucketing prefix_hash. We can also export a sample of cache keys (hashed) for hot-key inspection.
[05:42] Tom Brenner: what about quantized kernels? timings differ a lot on 8-bit runs. Can we see per-kernel timings?
[05:50] Ethan Zhao: yes we emit kernel-level spans (lightweight) for key ops: matmul, rmsnorm, softmax. For 8-bit quantized runs the kernel spans include quantization tag (q8, q4, etc.) and the measured ms. These are aggregated to avoid trace storming.
[06:18] Sarah Lim: hmm, for dashboards we'd like: P50/P95 per-route, per-model, token-cost per-call, cache hit ratio, batch-wait distribution, and a heatmap of hot prefixes. Any out-of-the-box dashboards?
[06:29] Lena Ortiz: Redwood console ships a starter dashboard for token-level telemetry and we can export JSON panels for Grafana. We'll attach the Grafana JSON and a sample BigQuery schema for cost analysis.
[07:00] Carlos Mendes: sampling again — do you recommend head sampling or probabilistic per-token?
[07:08] Ethan Zhao: combine approaches: head-sampling at 1% for short responses; for responses >500 tokens enable interval sampling (e.g., emit spans every 16 tokens) and tail sampling to always capture a small percentage of long tails. Tail-sampling is especially useful for regressions.
[07:44] Priya Rao: is there any way to redact or hash tokens before they are logged? we need PII protections.
[07:51] Maya Patel: yes – two options: 1) client-side prefiltering inside your VPC that strips tokens or replaces with salted hashes; 2) runtime-level hashing where Redwood emits token hashes with a customer-specific salt. We'll document both patterns and include sample code.
[08:22] Sarah Lim: operational question: latency SLO is 150ms P95 on typical queries. How does tracing overhead affect that?
[08:30] Ethan Zhao: tracers are async and non-blocking; per-span overhead is minimal but high-cardinality per-token spans can add CPU and network traffic. Our guidance: use aggregated metrics for SLOs and selective token-span sampling for root cause. With recommended configs, overhead is sub-2% for production workloads.
[08:59] Tom Brenner: what's the recommended batch_size for balancing throughput vs. latency? our experiments show batch sizes >8 hurt p95.
[09:07] Ethan Zhao: depends on model and GPU — Redwood supports dynamic batching; we recommend target latency SLO first then tune batch ceiling. For many Seq2Seq workloads we see good throughput with batch ceilings of 8-16; for high-latency-sensitive endpoints use batch ceiling 4. We'll share benchmark curves.
[09:38] Sarah Lim: Can you talk about fallback when Dedicated capacity is saturated? We run traffic spikes during events.
[09:44] Maya Patel: smart routing can fall back to a lower-capacity variant or hosted spare capacity. For the pilot we can set up a canary route that routes x% to a cheaper variant and monitor token-cost and latency. All of this is visible in the token telemetry.
[10:12] Carlos Mendes: what about OTEL attributes — do you recommend attaching full request metadata as attributes on every span? that's a lot.
[10:19] Ethan Zhao: prefer sparse attributes: request_id, route, model_id, batch_id, cache_hit boolean, and token_phase. Put heavy fields (prompt snippet) in a linked event only on sampled traces. Also leverage resource-level attributes for static tags.
[10:46] Sarah Lim: about KV cache eviction and prefetch—we see a periodic cold-snap where many prefixes miss after cache churn. Can instrumentation help pinpoint when eviction happens?
[10:54] Ethan Zhao: yes, emit eviction events as metrics and as a low-sample event stream. Correlate with batch heatmap and shard-level eviction counters. We'll provide a dashboard showing eviction frequency vs. demand to tune shard counts.
[11:22] Priya Rao: from a compliance perspective: can audit logs link a trace id to who accessed what model + when?
[11:29] Maya Patel: yes audit logs include request_id, user_id (if provided), model & route, and the operation. We can provide a signed audit bundle on request.
[11:48] Carlos Mendes: latency breakdown — we want to separate network enqueue, batch wait, GPU kernel time, sampling time. Is that doable?
[11:55] Ethan Zhao: absolutely — spans are arranged to reflect these phases. We produce waterfall charts in the console and attach span timings in OTEL so you can reconstruct the breakdown.
[12:20] Sarah Lim: excellent, can we do a quick live walk-through of a sample trace?
[12:25] Maya Patel: sure Ethan, do you have a demo trace?
[12:28] Ethan Zhao: yes I'll share a sanitized trace from a prior run — note some names/ids redacted.
[12:34] [12:34] Ethan Zhao: (screen share) you can see here the root span request/12345, child span enqueue, batch-dispatch with batch_id=42 and then kernel spans. At about 00:00:03.2 we have a big jump in kernel ms that corresponds to a cache miss.
[13:02] Sarah Lim: I see the batch index mapping, that helps. Can we map spans back to tenant ids to calculate per-tenant token costs?
[13:12] Ethan Zhao: yes, add tenant_id as an attribute; sums can be computed downstream by aggregating token count * model_cost_per_token. We recommend adding a request-level token_count metric to avoid per-token math in traces.
[13:38] Tom Brenner: what about synthetic load testing and trace fidelity under load?
[13:45] Ethan Zhao: we ran tests at 10x concurrency and tail-sampling held up. The collector backpressure needs tuning; use batch_processor with queued retry and adjust exporter timeouts.
[14:10] Sarah Lim: are there any known gotchas with OTLP exporters and private on-prem collectors?
[14:16] Ethan Zhao: yes the main ones: TLS handshake load on collector, buffer sizes causing increased memory, and attribute cardinality exploding tag cardinality in your backend. We'll include best-practices for the collector config.
[14:40] Maya Patel: quick pause — any legal procurement constraints we should note for pilot?
[14:45] Priya Rao: we have a standard DPA and want vendor SOC2 + ISO attestation, plus a penetration test report.
[14:52] Maya Patel: understood — we'll attach SOC2 cert and a data processing addendum.
[15:05] Carlos Mendes: if we hash tokens we need to ensure deterministic salt per-tenant, is that supported?
[15:12] Ethan Zhao: yes we can accept customer-supplied salt via KMS-protected config, and hashes are deterministic per-tenant.
[15:30] Sarah Lim: about dashboards — can you create a Grafana dashboard that has per-tenant cost and P95 latency side-by-side?
[15:37] Lena Ortiz: yes we can provide a starter Grafana dashboard and JSON panels; we'll also show a BigQuery example to compute cost by tenant.
[15:55] Tom Brenner: security — if we run Redwood Private in our VPC, who has access to the control plane?
[16:01] Maya Patel: control plane access is customer-managed; Redwood operators don't get data-plane access unless explicitly granted for troubleshooting. For Dedicated we offer elevated support with audit trails.
[16:25] Sarah Lim: sample size question — for cost modeling do you recommend simulating long tails?
[16:31] Ethan Zhao: yes, simulate long-tail completions and use tail-sampling to capture those cases. We can run a synthetic workload to estimate token distribution and unit cost.
[17:00] Carlos Mendes: what about real-time alerting for sudden cache churn?
[17:05] Lena Ortiz: create an alert on sudden drop in cache hit ratio or spike in eviction rate; Redwood console can push to PagerDuty/Slack.
[17:22] Sarah Lim: okay, next steps?
[17:25] Maya Patel: here's what we'll do: Ethan will share the OTLP collector config + sanitized trace example, Lena will share Grafana panels and dashboard JSON, and I'll send pilot pricing and security pack. We'll aim to start staging trace capture by next week.
[17:45] Priya Rao: can you include the option to not send prompt text and only hashed tokens in the config?
[17:51] Maya Patel: yes we'll include a redaction option in the sample config.
[18:10] Sarah Lim: timeline — we want a 2-week eval, then expand to pilot. Are you able to support quick bench runs?
[18:17] Maya Patel: yes SE-led bench runs are included in the pilot scope. We'll need staging creds and an agreed test plan.
[18:35] Tom Brenner: ok great — any final clarifications?
[18:40] Carlos Mendes: one more on batch index mapping — how stable is that across restarts? we want reproducibility.
[18:45] Ethan Zhao: batch_index is ephemeral per-batch, but we also emit request_id and sequence numbers so you can reorder traces. We can provide a match table for post-processing.
[19:06] Sarah Lim: perfect. Thanks everyone.
[19:10] Maya Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts and schedule the staging capture.
[54:30] (meeting end)
